clue.text: Varnish explosive account

parts.note: a shell is an explosive artillery projectile

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper describes a varnished report as dynamite.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin dissolved in alcohol and brushed on wood as a glossy protective coating.

clue.text: Previously mentioned eating pea, reportedly tasty

indicators.note: the word for mentioned earlier takes the letter in, swallowing it

parts.note: said, as in the said person, means mentioned before

indicators.note: said aloud, the vegetable is the name of a letter

parts.note: a pea is the green vegetable

explanation.surface: A report that eating the pea already mentioned was tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid is a literary word for having a pleasant flavour, the opposite of insipid.

clue.text: Poles are nowhere near this European cod quota, right?

indicators.note: cod means fake or mock, so these letters are a sham version of the word

explanation.surface: Polish fishermen are far from the EU cod quota, aren't they?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like Polish people, and 'cod' like the fish; the Poles are the Earth's ends and 'cod' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The line round the Earth's middle is as far as anywhere can be from the North and South Poles.

clue.text: Reluctant bunch beginning to hesitate

parts.note: a lot is a group or bunch

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A group reluctant to begin, holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: Loth, also spelt loath, means unwilling or disinclined.

clue.text: Wrapping up a carp order, get dizzy

indicators.note: a dizzy head spins, so these letters whirl into a new order

explanation.surface: Packing a fish to order leaves someone giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrapping up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' is part of the fodder and 'Wrapping' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridged cardboard sheets are used as packaging, protecting goods inside a parcel.

clue.text: Three times donning winter gear in part of Caribbean

indicators.note: the skis put on the three letters like clothing, so those letters end up inside them
the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: skis are kit for snowy winter sport
the first of three T's, each the abbreviation for time
the remaining two T's of the three, T being short for time

explanation.surface: Someone wraps up three times over in ski clothing before a Caribbean trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Ts are not together: one goes after the first S and two after the I, giving S-T-KI-TT-S.
explanation.definitionFit: The island is one half of the federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis in the Leeward Islands of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Short dominatrix may have done this

definitions.meaning: being short means lacking enough money
a dominatrix may have bound a client with straps in order to be paid

explanation.surface: A short dominatrix and her professional habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally: someone tied up with straps for the sake of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hard up or broke is being short; the literal reading pictures binding a client in exchange for payment.

clue.text: Reprimanded Kelvin and editor over fish catch

indicators.note: the two outside letters spread over the fish and catch, enclosing them

parts.note: K is the symbol for kelvin, the unit of temperature
an eel is a fish
a haul is a catch of fish

explanation.surface: Lord Kelvin and an editor go fishing, then get told off.
explanation.walkthrough: Keelhauling was a naval punishment of dragging someone under a ship's keel; figuratively it means a severe rebuke.
explanation.definitionFit: The old punishment came to mean figuratively rebuking someone harshly, as when an employee is hauled over the coals.

clue.text: Chaos in Timor university upset student

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, so the letters are tumbled into a new order

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Turmoil at a university in Timor after a student is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disorder and confusion.

clue.text: Outre punishment accepted by Bond?

indicators.note: the agent takes the beating into his own name, holding it inside

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional British spy
a lash is a stroke of the whip

explanation.surface: James Bond takes an unusual beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Splashy means flamboyant or showy, close to outre, eccentric and over the top.

clue.text: Leo and Rupert nobbled dealer in game

indicators.note: a nobbled racehorse has been tampered with, so these letters have been interfered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Two men fix a race against a rival who deals in game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A poulterer is a shopkeeper selling poultry and game such as pheasant, grouse and rabbit.

clue.text: Corrupt US corporation contracts left in register

indicators.note: the company name shrinks by losing its final letter

parts.note: Enron was the US energy company that collapsed in an accounting fraud in 2001

explanation.surface: A dodgy American firm puts its paperwork, signed contracts, on the official register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' looks like a noun for legal agreements but is a verb here: shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to put one's name on a roll or list, the verb sense of register.

clue.text: See fruit become outmoded

definitions.meaning: to see someone is to go out with them romantically
the sweet brown fruit of a palm tree

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at fruit that is going past its best.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense is a dictionary meaning: courting someone, a palm fruit, and growing old-fashioned.

clue.text: Hound minorities?

parts.note: minority can mean the state of being under age, so a dog's minority is the time before it is fully grown

explanation.surface: Reads like a call to persecute minority groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' looks like a verb meaning harass; it is a noun, and 'minorities' means periods of being a minor.
explanation.definitionFit: Each young dog passes through a stage of being a pup, its minority before adulthood.

clue.text: Hit dumbly on me and Mo

indicators.note: letters that are hit are knocked about, so they are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone struck mutely, perhaps by two people named Mo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mo' looks like a short name; it is the chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Mo is the symbol on the periodic table for this metallic element, atomic number 42.

clue.text: Dares holy man to shed clothes and nipple ring

indicators.note: each word strips off its outer letters, as if undressing, leaving only its middle

explanation.surface: A dare to a priest to strip off, with a piercing thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: The areola is the pigmented circle of skin around the nipple, so literally a ring around it.

clue.text: Just as stormy after wind has backed

indicators.note: a wind backs when it shifts anticlockwise, as from south to east, so the compass letter for south becomes the one for east

parts.note: squally weather has sudden violent gusts

explanation.surface: A weather report: just as rough as before once the wind shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: Backing is a sailor's term for a wind turning anticlockwise; south to east is such a turn, so S gives way to E.
explanation.definitionFit: Equally and just as both mean to the same degree, as in equally good or just as good.

clue.text: Preserve key old photo

parts.note: to tin food is to preserve it in a can
to key text is to type it

explanation.surface: Instructions to keep safe an important old photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A tintype was a nineteenth-century photograph made directly on a thin sheet of iron.

clue.text: Name a record in Filipino language!

parts.note: a tag is a name or label
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: Instructions to label a record in Filipino.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagalog is the main language of the Philippines and the basis of Filipino, its national language.

clue.text: Falls once more, back on uppers in real adversity

indicators.note: in a down answer back means the word runs from bottom to top

parts.note: again means once more

indicators.note: the upper letters, the first ones, of each word

explanation.surface: Someone falls again, then is back on their feet despite hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' looks like a verb but names the waterfalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls are the famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border, often called simply Niagara.

clue.text: Ruffle Shylock, collecting this sort of payment?

indicators.note: the two words gather the letters up between them, across the gap

explanation.surface: Upsetting Shylock, the moneylender of The Merchant of Venice, as he comes to take his pound of flesh.
explanation.walkthrough: Shylock's bond demands a pound of flesh, so a payment of that sort is a fleshy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock's bond asks for a pound of his debtor's body, a payment literally made of flesh.

clue.text: The rich claiming right to endless produce

indicators.note: the wealthy take the letter for right into their midst

parts.note: the haves are the wealthy, as in haves and have-nots

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: The wealthy claim the right to endless farm produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' looks like a verb but is the noun: a harvest is what a crop yields.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is the crop gathered in a season, the yield or produce of the land.

clue.text: Brahms and Liszt arranged opus as entirely sung piece

indicators.note: rhyming slang for pissed, meaning drunk, so the letters reel about into a new order

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus in music catalogues

explanation.surface: Two Romantic composers rework an opus into something fully sung.
explanation.walkthrough: The composers are not people here: Brahms and Liszt is British rhyming slang for drunk, the anagram signal, and 'arranged' is fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of opera has every word sung, with no spoken dialogue, unlike operetta or opéra comique.

clue.text: Crop of unrefined cocaine going west

indicators.note: in an across answer west is the left, so the drug's letter travels to the front

parts.note: raw means unprocessed
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A shipment of crude cocaine heads westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crop' looks like a harvest, fitting the drug scene, but it is the pouch in a bird's gullet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's crop is a pouch in its throat for storing food, also called its craw.

clue.text: Ring supremo of security group with backing

indicators.note: in a down answer backing means the letters climb from bottom to top

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a security alliance

explanation.surface: A boxing promoter running a security firm with financial backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests boxing; it is Wagner's Ring cycle of operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Wotan is the chief of the gods in Wagner's Ring cycle, the German form of Odin.

clue.text: Absolutely nothing about French and Greek cheese

indicators.note: the nothing goes round the French word

parts.note: FA is short for sweet FA, British slang for nothing at all
et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: French and Greek cheeses compared, and found utterly wanting.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is the white brined cheese of Greece, made from sheep or goat milk.

clue.text: Find out Heath harboured this royal knight

parts.note: King Lear wanders on the heath in Shakespeare's play
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: Discovering that Edward Heath, the former prime minister, sheltered a royal knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heath' looks like Edward Heath, the British prime minister, but it is the stormy heath of King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn a fact is to discover or find it out.

clue.text: Job of textile workers, in part

indicators.note: the workers sit inside the abbreviation

parts.note: lacemen made or dealt in lace

explanation.surface: A post among cloth workers, part-time perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A placement is a position found for someone, a posting or job, often temporary.

clue.text: Butter spread round school

indicators.note: turning the pair round means reading them from the end back to the start

parts.note: a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter
marg is short for margarine, a bread spread

explanation.surface: Butter being spread on bread at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the dairy product, but it is one who butts, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammar is a British selective secondary school, short for grammar school.

clue.text: Listen to number and cheer up

parts.note: to hear is to listen to
ten is a number

explanation.surface: An instruction to heed a number and feel cheered.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to encourage them and lift their spirits.
